{{Short description|Internet protocol}}'''Garlic routing'''<ref name="urlHow to Browse the Internet Anonymously with Garlic Routing - Make Tech Easier">{{cite web |url=https://www.maketecheasier.com/garlic-routing-browse-internet-anonymously/ |title=How to Browse the Internet Anonymously with Garlic Routing - Make Tech Easier |format= |date=21 August 2019 |accessdate=}}</ref> is a variant of [[onion routing]] that encrypts multiple messages together to make it more difficult<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://privacy-pc.com/articles/common-darknet-weaknesses-an-overview-of-attack-strategies.html|title=Common Darknet Weaknesses: An Overview of Attack Strategies|first=David|last=B|date=January 27, 2014}}</ref> for attackers to perform [[traffic analysis]] while also increasing the speed of [[data transfer]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zantour|first1=Bassam|last2=Haraty|first2=Ramzi A.|title=I2P Data Communication System|journal=Proceedings of ICN 2011: The Tenth International Conference on Networks|date=2011|pages=401–409}}</ref>

[[Michael J. Freedman]] defined garlic routing as an extension of onion routing, in which multiple messages are bundled together. He called each message a "bulb", whereas I2P calls them "[[garlic]] cloves."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://geti2p.net/en/docs/how/garlic-routing|title=Garlic Routing and "Garlic" Terminology|website=geti2p.net|language=en|access-date=2025-08-23}}</ref> All messages, each with their own delivery instructions, are exposed at the endpoint. This enables efficient bundling of an onion routing reply block with the original message.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freehaven.net/doc/oreilly/freehaven-ch12.html|title=Peer-To-Peer: Harnessing the Power of Disruptive Technologies...Chapter 12: Free Haven|last1=Freedman|first1=Michael|first2=Roger|last2=Dingledine|website=freehaven.net|language=en|access-date=2025-08-23}}</ref>

Garlic routing is one of the key factors that distinguishes [[I2P]] from [[Tor (anonymity network)|Tor]] and other privacy-focused or [[encryption]] networks. The name alludes to the [[garlic]] plant, whose multi-layered structure this protocol resembles. "Garlic routing" was coined by Michael J. Freedman in [[Roger Dingledine]]'s Free Haven Master's thesis Section 8.1.1 (June 2000), as derived from [[Onion routing|Onion Routing]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://geti2p.net/en/docs/how/garlic-routing|title=Garlic Routing - I2P|website=geti2p.net}}</ref> However, the garlic routing implementation in [[I2P]] differs from the design proposed by Freedman. The key distinction is that garlic routing used unidirectional tunnels, while mainstream alternatives like [[Tor (anonymity network)|Tor]] and [[Mixmaster anonymous remailer|Mixmaster]] use bidirectional tunnels.

== Garlic Cast: Lightweight and Decentralized Content Sharing ==
One potential implementation of the garlic routing protocol is shown in the paper ''Garlic Cast: Lightweight and Decentralized Anonymous Content Sharing''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://login.microsoftonline.com/7cf48d45-3ddb-4389-a9c1-c115526eb52e/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?response_type=code&scope=openid%20profile&client_id=f08a1f95-66f7-4194-8032-2c3ec54d478c&state=u9I_d9MJVyJHZQgYYSvqbp5vrc4&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fscripts.libraries.psu.edu%2Foidc%2Fredirect&nonce=_Mee2W25y_1ch8Xa-_2763rxRTybocT2EBDEVdMljtU&domain_hint=psu.edu|title=Penn State WebAccess Secure Login|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref>  The idea is to provide a resilient and low latency anonymous content sharing network based on garlic routing.  The distinguishing benefit that makes the system different from traditional [[Tor (anonymity network)|Tor]] networks is that it is designed around secure, fast communication.  This is achieved by allowing the Garlic Cast system to use random walks to find proxies in the overlay network, then applying a security-enhanced Information Dispersal Algorithm to deliver content efficiently and securely.<ref name=":0" />  Lastly, the Garlic Cast network is designed to resist a wide range of attacks while maintaining a high level of anonymity.<ref name="urlGarlic Cast: Lightweight and Decentralized Anonymous Content Sharing | Semantic Scholar">{{cite book |year=2016 |doi=10.1109/ICPADS.2016.0037 |s2cid=5544561 |last1=Qian |first1=Chen |last2=Shi |first2=Junjie |last3=Yu |first3=Zihao |last4=Yu |first4=Ye |last5=Zhong |first5=Sheng |title=2016 IEEE 22nd International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems (ICPADS) |chapter=Garlic Cast: Lightweight and Decentralized Anonymous Content Sharing |pages=216–223 |isbn=978-1-5090-4457-3 }}</ref>

==List of P2P applications that use garlic routing==
* [[I2P]], an anonymizing [[overlay network]] that allows applications to run on top of it (open-source, written in Java)
* [[Perfect Dark (P2P)|Perfect Dark]], a P2P client which relies on a [[Mix network|mixnet]] and [[distributed file system|distributed datastore]] to provide anonymity (freeware, written for [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]])
